(see Theorem 2.14) Suppose $G$ is an arbitrary smooth affine $k$ -group scheme. If we consider $X=\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2}$ equipped with the flag $D=\mathbb{A}^{1}=\{y=0\}$, $Z=\{x=y=0\}:=\underline{0}$, then there are canonical isomorphisms of fppf sheaves of sets

(0.9)

${}^{L}\mathcal{G}r_{G}\simeq{}^{L}\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}_{G;(\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2},\mathbb{A}^{1},\underline{0})} \mathcal{G}r^{\mathrm{big}}_{G}\simeq\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}_{G;(\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2},\mathbb{A}^{1},\underline{0})}^{\mathrm{big}} \mathcal{G}r^{J}_{G}\simeq\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}_{G;(\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2},\mathbb{A}^{1},\underline{0})}^{J} \mathcal{G}r^{\mathrm{(2)}}_{G}\simeq\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}^{(2)}_{G;(\mathbb{A}^{2}_{k},\mathbb{A}^{1},\underline{0})}.$

Note that Theorem B does not mention the geometric Grassmannian for the loop group $\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}_{G;(\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2},\mathbb{A}^{1},\underline{0})}^{L}$. Indeed, for this, we are only able to prove that it agrees with its two-variables quotient cousin $\mathcal{G}r^{L}_{G}$ on $k$ -points for $G$ special or solvable (Proposition 2.16). Note that, in particular, Theorem B says that for $(X,D,Z)=(\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2},\mathbb{A}^{1},\underline{0})$ all the fppf stacks in (0.8), except possibly $\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}_{G;(X,D,Z)}^{L}$, are actually ind-representable fppf sheaves of sets. The proof of Theorem B proceeds by analyzing each case separately.

paper.title: Two dimensional versions of the affine Grassmannian and their geometric description
paper.abstract: For a smooth affine algebraic group $G$ over an algebraically closed field, we consider several two-variables generalizations of the affine Grassmannian $G(\!(t)\!)/G[\![t]\!]$, given by quotients of the double loop group $G(\!(x)\!)(\!(y)\!)$. We prove that they are representable by ind-schemes if $G$ is solvable. Given a smooth surface $X$ and a flag of subschemes of $X$, we provide a geometric interpretation of the two-variables Grassmannians, in terms of bundles and trivialisation data defined on appropriate loci in $X$, which depend on the flag.
